highlights: July 16, 1969: Apollo 11 launched on a Saturn V rocket from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon at 10:56 p.m. EDT on July 20, 1969; Buzz Aldrin followed about 19 minutes later.
Their only moonwalk lasted about 2 hours 31 minutes, and they never went more than about 100 meters from Eagle.
Eagle's crew spent about 21.5 hours on the surface before the ascent stage lifted off on July 21, 1969.
July 24, 1969: the crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean, completing the first Moon landing mission.

It sat about 17 meters south of Eagle as part of EASEP, a 48 kg kit that also held a dust detector.
August 3, 1969: controllers turned it off before its first lunar sunset because its solar power was fading.
It woke up again for a second lunar day, but stopped obeying commands in late August 1969.

August 1, 1969: Lick Observatory in California caught the first laser echoes from it.
Its 100 fused-silica corner cubes are each about 3.8 cm across, about the size of a golf ball.
Laser stations such as Apache Point in New Mexico and Grasse in France still aim at it today.

highlights: November 14, 1969: lightning struck Apollo 12's Saturn V twice during launch, but the crew reset the power and flew on.
Intrepid landed in the Ocean of Storms on November 19, 1969, at 06:54 UT.
Conrad and Bean made two moonwalks totaling about 7 hours 45 minutes.
The first color TV camera on the Moon broke early when it was accidentally pointed at the Sun.
The crew brought home about 34 kg of rocks and soil, plus parts of Surveyor 3.

highlights: November 19, 1969: Bean and Conrad set it up on their first moonwalk, about 130 meters from Intrepid.
Its SNAP-27 nuclear generator made about 70 watts, a little more than a bright light bulb uses.
Its instruments included a seismometer, a magnetometer, a solar wind spectrometer and an ion detector.
April 1970: it felt the Apollo 13 rocket stage crash about 135 km away and rang for hours.

Controllers then jettisoned it and fired its engine to send it down, hitting the Moon on November 20 at 22:17 UT.

November 20, 1969: Conrad and Bean walked to it on their second moonwalk and cut off its camera and scoop.
Scientists reported Earth germs inside its camera, but later reviews suggest they got in after it came home.

April 17, 1970: the crew splashed down safely in the Pacific, two days after this stage hit the Moon.

Antares landed at Fra Mauro on February 5, 1971, at 09:18 UT.
Alan Shepard, age 47, was the only Mercury astronaut to walk on the Moon.
The crew's two moonwalks lasted about 9 hours 22 minutes in total.
LRO images later showed they came within about 30 meters of Cone crater's rim without knowing it.

A mortar box with small grenades was meant to make later moonquakes, but it was never fired.
Like Apollo 12's station, it ran on a SNAP-27 plutonium generator, so it worked day and night.

highlights: July 26, 1971: Apollo 15 launched carrying the heaviest Apollo payload yet, including the first lunar rover.

Before walking, Dave Scott stood up through the top hatch to survey the landing site.
Three moonwalks lasted about 18.5 hours, and the crew brought home about 77 kg of samples.
August 1971: the crew left a small 'Fallen Astronaut' statue and plaque honoring astronauts who had died.

A navigation system tracked direction and distance so the crew could always find the way back to Falcon.
The rover was built by Boeing and runs on two non-rechargeable silver-zinc batteries.

Its plutonium generator kept it running through about six years of lunar nights.

The crew set up the first telescope on the Moon, a far-ultraviolet camera built by George Carruthers.
John Young leaped off the ground while saluting the flag, a famous photo from April 21, 1972.

Three moonwalks lasted about 22 hours, the longest of any Apollo mission.
The crew stayed on the Moon for about 75 hours, also an Apollo record.
December 19, 1972: the crew splashed down in the Pacific, ending the Apollo Moon landings.

The map-and-tape fender patch came home and is now in the Smithsonian's collection.
